metadata.case_name: TAM PANG v. WONG PIT CHUNG

plaintiff.occupation_before: ran a small-scale family-type business recycling old cement bags by refashioning them as wrappings for fish

source: the injuries suffered by the plaintiff, for which he was treated in hospital, were a two lacerations of the scalp; b subtrochanteric fracture of right femur (i.e. the hip); c fracture of left tibia and fibula (i.e. the leg).
Those two lacerations of the scalp were sutured, and have completely healed, the only remaining effect of them now being a 3" scar on the scalp which is obscured by hair.

injuries.description: subtrochanteric fracture of right femur (i.e. the hip)
source: the injuries suffered by the plaintiff, for which he was treated in hospital, were a two lacerations of the scalp; b subtrochanteric fracture of right femur (i.e. the hip); c fracture of left tibia and fibula (i.e. the leg).

The subtrochanteric fracture was treated initially with skeletal traction as the plaintiff had an extensive rash, which was diagnosed by a dermatologist as psoriasis, and that too had to be treated. An open reduction of this fracture was done with the insertion of a nail, plate and screws on 20th June 1977.

The fracture of the right femur is well united, but he has finished up with some restriction of movement of the right hip joint. He can now only bend that leg at the hip through 110o instead of the usual 140o and external rotation is reduced from the normal 50o to 20o.
As the result of the accident his left leg finished up shortened by 7/8ths of an inch and the right leg by about ¼".

injuries.description: fracture of left tibia and fibula (i.e. the leg)
source: the injuries suffered by the plaintiff, for which he was treated in hospital, were a two lacerations of the scalp; b subtrochanteric fracture of right femur (i.e. the hip); c fracture of left tibia and fibula (i.e. the leg).
The fractures of the left tibia and fibula were treated by closed reduction and plaster of Paris immobilization for 10 weeks.
The union of the fractures of the left leg is sound and the alignment excellent.
As the result of the accident his left leg finished up shortened by 7/8ths of an inch and the right leg by about ¼".

the only effect of this is a prominent swelling on the side of the thigh.
